questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} - 2x + 2 = 0,$ then the least value of $n$ for which \left(\dfrac{α}{β}\right)n = 1$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$x^{2} - 2x + 2 = 0$

$⇒{( x - 1 )}^{2} + 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = 1 \pm i, i = \sqrt{- 1}$

Now let the roots $\alpha = i + i \text{ and } \beta = 1 - i$

\left(\dfrac{α}{β}\right)n = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)n = \left(\dfrac{i\left(1 - i\right)}{1 - i}\right)n$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{α}{β}\right)n = {( i )}^{n}$

Using given information,

$⇒ {( i )}^{n} = 1$

$⇒$ The minimum value of $n \in N = 4$~because~\left(i\right)4 = 1$.

questions.q: Let a complex number $z, \left|z\right| \ne 1$,~satisfy $log\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|z\right| + 11}{\left(\left|z\right| - 1\right)2}\right) \le 2$. Then, the largest~value of~\left|z\right|$ is equal to _________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$log\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|z\right| + 11}{\left(\left|z\right| - 1\right)2}\right) \le 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|z\right| + 11}{\left(\left|z\right| - 1\right)2} \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$,~\left\{∵ \log_{\mathrm{a}}\left(b\right) \le c ⇒ b \ge a^{c}if0 < a < 1\right\}$

$⇒ 2\left|z\right| + 22 \ge \left(\left|z\right| - 1\right)2$,~\left\{∵ \left|z\right| \ne 1 \text{ and } \left(\left|z\right| - 1\right)2 > 0\right\}$

$⇒ 2\left|z\right| + 22 \ge \left|z\right|2 + 1 - 2\left|z\right|$

$⇒ \left|z\right|2 - 4\left|z\right| - 21 \le 0$

$⇒ \left(\left|z\right| - 7\right)\left(\left|z\right| + 3\right) \le 0$

$⇒ \left|z\right| \le 7$

$∴$ Largest value of \left|z\right|$ is $7$

$

questions.q: The complex number $z = \dfrac{i - 1}{cos\dfrac{π}{3} + isin\dfrac{π}{3}}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$z = \dfrac{i - 1}{cos\dfrac{π}{3} + isin\dfrac{π}{3}}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2}\right)}{cos\dfrac{π}{3} + isin\dfrac{π}{3}}$

Now argument of complex number~$\dfrac{- 1}{2} + \dfrac{i}{2}$~is~$\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

So, by euler's formula~$e^{i\theta} = cos\theta + isin\theta$~we get,

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{i3\pi / 4}}{ei\pi / 3}$

$⇒ z = \sqrt{2}e^{i5\pi / 12}$

$⇒ z = \sqrt{2} \lleft(cos\dfrac{5\pi}{12} ++isin\dfrac{5\pi}{12})

$

questions.q: If $a$ and $b$ are real numbers such that \left(2 + \alpha\right)4 = a + b\alpha$, where $\alpha = \dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$, then $a + b$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
& \left(2 + \alpha\right){}^{4} = a + b\alpha$
\left(4 + {α}^{2} + 4\alpha\right)2 = a + b\alpha$

Now using,~$\alpha = \dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2} ⇒ \lleft(2\alpha +1)2 = \lleft(i\sqrt{3})2$

$⇒ {α}^{2} = - \left(1 + \alpha\right)$

So,~$a + b\alpha = \left(4 - \alpha -1 + 4\alpha\right)2$

$a + b\alpha = \left($3 + $3\alpha\right)$2 = 9 \left(1 + 2\alpha + {α}^{2}\right)$
$a + b\alpha =$=9\left(1 + 2\alpha + \left(-1 - \alpha\right)\right) =$=9\alpha$

$⇒ a = 0, b = 9 ⇒ a + b = 9$

$

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of the equation $x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$, then ${α}^{2021} + {β}^{2021} + {γ}^{2021} + {δ}^{2021}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that& $x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$~can be written as~

$\dfrac{x^{5} - 1}{x - 1} = 0⇒ x^{5} = 1$

i.e.~$x = \left(1\right)\dfrac{1}{5}$

So $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $\delta$ are the ${5}^{th }$ roots of unity except $1$.

Now, from the concept of~roots of unity, we know

~${α}^{n} + {β}^{n} + {γ}^{n} + {δ}^{n} + {1}^{n} = \left\{$\begin{cases}0 & \text{if}n\text{is not a multiple of}5 \\ 5 & \text{if}n\text{ is a multiple of}5\end{cases}$\right

So,~${α}^{2021} + {β}^{2021} + {γ}^{2021} + {δ}^{2021} = - 1$.

questions.q: If the real part of the complex number \left(1 - cos\theta + 2isin\theta\right)- 1$ is $\dfrac{1}{5}$ for $\theta \in ( 0, \pi ) ,$~then the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{θ}sinxdx$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$z = \dfrac{1}{1 - cos\theta + 2isin\theta}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\left(1 - cos\theta\right) - 2isin\theta}{\left(1 - cos\theta + 2isin\theta\right)\left(1 - cos\theta - 2isin\theta\right)}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) - 2isin\theta}{( 1 - cos\theta{)}^{2} + 4\sin^{2}\theta}$

Put,$sin\theta = 2sin\dfrac{θ}{2}cos\dfrac{θ}{2}, 1 - cos\theta = 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) - 4isin\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)\cos \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)}{4\sin^{4}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 16\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)}$

Hence,

$Re\left(z\right) = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)}{4\sin^{4}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 16\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 8\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 8\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) = \dfrac{5}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) + 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) = \dfrac{5}{2}$

$⇒ 3\cos^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{θ}{2} = n\pi \pm \dfrac{π}{4}, n \in Z$

$⇒ \theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{π}{2}$

For~$\theta \in ( 0, \pi )$,~$\theta = \dfrac{π}{2}$.

Hence,

$∴ {∫}_{0}^{θ}sin\thetad\theta = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}sin\thetad\theta = {- cos\theta}_{0}^{\pi2}$

$= - \left(0 - 1\right)$

$= 1

$

questions.q: Let ${z}_{0}$ be a root of quadratic equation, $x^{2} + x + 1 = 0 .$ If $z = 3 + 6i{z}_{0}^{81} - 3i{z}_{0}^{93}$ , then $arg  \left(z\right) is equal to:$

questions.solution:
${z}_{0} = w$ or $w^{2}$

When ${z}_{0} = w$

$z = 3 + 6i \times w^{81} - 3i \times w^{93}$

$= 3 + 6i - 3i = 3 + 3i$

When ${z}_{0} = w^{2}$

$z = 3 + 6i \times {\left(w^{2}\right)}^{81} - 3i \times {\left(w^{2}\right)}^{93}$

$= 3 + 6i - 3i = 3 + 3i$

$∴ arg \left(z\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{Im\left(z\right)}{Re\left(z\right)}\right) = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{3}{3}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4}$

questions.q:
For $a \in \mathbb{C}$, let $A = { z \in \mathbb{C}: Re ( a + \overset{¯}{z} ) > Im ( \overset{¯}{a} + z ) }$ and $B = { z \in \mathbb{C}: Re ( a + \overset{¯}{z} ) < Im ( \overset{¯}{a} + z ) }$. Then among the two statements:
$( S1 )$ : If $Re ( a ) , Im ( a ) > 0$, then the set $A$ contains all the real numbers
$( S2 )$ : If $Re ( a ) , Im ( a ) < 0$, then the set $B$ contains all the real numbers,
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $a = {x}_{1} + i{y}_{1}, \overset{¯}{a} = {x}_{1} - i{y}_{1}$

And~$z = {x}_{2} + i{y}_{2}, \overset{¯}{z} = {x}_{2} - i{y}_{2}$~ ~

Now,

$a + \overset{¯}{z} = \left({x}_{1} + {x}_{2}\right) +i \left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)

and~$\overset{¯}{a} + z = \left({x}_{1} + {x}_{2}\right) +$i \left({y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right)$

Now according to the question,

$Re ( a + \overset{¯}{z} ) = {x}_{1} + {x}_{2}$~and

$Im ( \overset{¯}{a} + z ) = {y}_{2} - {y}_{1}$

$A = \left\{z: {x}_{1} + {x}_{2} > {y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right\} = \left\{z: {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} + {x}_{2} > {y}_{2}\right\}$
~ $B = \left\{z: {x}_{1} + {x}_{2} < {y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right\} = \left\{z: {x}_{1} + {y}_{1} + {x}_{2} < {y}_{2}\right\}$

If ${y}_{2} = 0$~and~${x}_{1}, {y}_{1} > 0$~then

$A = { z: {x}_{2} > - \left({x}_{1} + {y}_{1}\right) }$

A covers a part of negative real axis and therefore, does not contain whole real axis

Similarly if~${y}_{2} = 0$, and~${x}_{1}, {y}_{1} < 0$, then~
$B = { z: {x}_{2} < - \left({x}_{1} + {y}_{1}\right) }$
$∴$~$B& covers part of positive real axis and therefore does not cover whole real axis.

Hence, both are false.

$

questions.q: If \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} =  \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} =1, \left(m, n \in N\right)$~then the greatest common divisor of the least values of $m$ and $n$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

Rationalize both the terms

\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i} \times \dfrac{1 + i}{1 + i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1} \times \dfrac{- 1 - i}{- 1 - i}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

\left(\dfrac{1 + i^{2} + 2i}{1 - i^{2}}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{- 1 - i^{2} - 2i}{\left(- 1\right)2 - i^{2}}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

We know~$i^{2} = - 1$

\left(\dfrac{2i}{2}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{- 2i}{2}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

\left(i\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(- i\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

For~\left(i\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{m}{2} = 4k ⇒ m = 8k, k \in I$

Since~$m$~is natural number so the least value of~$m$~is~$8$.

For~\left(- i\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{n}{3} = 4l ⇒ n = 12l, l \in I$

Since~$n$~is natural number so the least value of~$n$~is~$12$.

So greatest common factor of~$8$~and~$12$~is~$4$.

$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2-a x-b=0$ with $\operatorname{Im}(\alpha) \lt \operatorname{Im}(\beta)$. Let $P_n=\alpha^n-\beta^n$. If $\mathrm{P}_3=-5 \sqrt{7} i, \mathrm{P}_4=-3 \sqrt{7} i, \mathrm{P}_5=11 \sqrt{7} i$ and $\mathrm{P}_6=45 \sqrt{7} i$, then \left|\alpha^4+\beta^4\right|$ is equal to $\qquad$ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha+\beta=\mathrm{a} \quad \alpha \beta=-\mathrm{b} \\
& \mathrm{P}_6=\mathrm{aP}_5+\mathrm{bP}_4 \\
& 45 \sqrt{7} \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{a} \times 11 \sqrt{7} \mathrm{i}+\mathrm{b}(-3 \sqrt{7}) \mathrm{i} \\
& 45=11 \mathrm{a}-3 \mathrm{~b}
\end{aligned}$
and
$\begin{aligned}
& P_5=\mathrm{aP}_4+b P_3 \\
& 11 \sqrt{7} \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{a}(-3 \sqrt{7} \mathrm{i})+\mathrm{b}(-5 \sqrt{7} \mathrm{i}) \\
& 11=-3 \mathrm{a}-5 \mathrm{~b} \\
& \mathrm{a}=3, \mathrm{~b}=-4 \\
& \left|\alpha^4+\beta^4\right|=\sqrt{\left(\alpha^4-\beta^4\right)^2+4 \alpha^4 \beta^4} \\
& =\sqrt{-63+4.4^4} \\
& =\sqrt{-63+1024}=\sqrt{961}=31
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $z = \dfrac{1 - i\sqrt{3}}{2}, i = \sqrt{- 1}$. Then the value of~$21 + \left(z + \dfrac{1}{z}\right)3 + \left(z^{2} + \dfrac{1}{z2}\right)3 + \left(z^{3} + \dfrac{1}{z3}\right)3 + \ldots + \left(z^{21} + \dfrac{1}{z21}\right)3$& is______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$z = \dfrac{1 - i\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ z = - \left(\dfrac{- 1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)

$⇒ z = - $\omega

where,~\omega~is the cube root of unity. So,

$1 + $\omega + {ω}^{2} =$0$

${ω}^{3} = 1$

Now, let

$A = \left($z + $\dfrac{1}{z}\right)$3 + \left($z^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{z2}\right)$3 + \left($z^{3} + $\dfrac{1}{z3}\right)$3 + \ldots + \left($z^{21} + $\dfrac{1}{z21}\right)$3$

$⇒ A = \left(- \omega - \dfrac{1}{ω}\right)$3 + \left({ω}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{\omega2}\right)$3 + \left(- {ω}^{3} - \dfrac{1}{\omega3}\right)$3 + \ldots . + \left(- {ω}^{21} - \dfrac{1}{\omega21}\right)$3$

$⇒ A = - \left(\dfrac{{ω}^{2} + 1}{ω}\right)$3 + \left(\dfrac{{ω}^{4} + 1}{\omega2}\right)$3 + \left(-$1 - $\dfrac{1}{1}\right)$3 + \ldots . + \left(- {ω}^{21} - \dfrac{1}{\omega21}\right)$3$

$⇒ A = - \left(\dfrac{- \omega}{ω}\right)$3 + \left(\dfrac{- {ω}^{2}}{\omega2}\right)$3 + \left(-$1 - 1\right)3 + \ldots . + \left(- {ω}^{21} - \dfrac{1}{\omega21}\right)$3$

$⇒ A = 1 + \left(-$1\right) + \left(-$1 - 1\right)3 + 1 + \left(-$1\right) + \left(-$1 - 1\right)3 \ldots . + \left(-$1 - 1\right)3$

$⇒ A = 3\left[$1 + \left(-$1\right)\right] + \left(-$1 - 1\right)3$

$⇒ A = - 8$

Then,

$21 + A = 21 - 8$

$= 13$

$
